transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve messed everything up. Like at work, I’ve been falling behind, and then the apartment stuff got out of hand too—sorry, it’s hard to explain, it all sort of connects in my head. I keep thinking I’ve ruined things for everyone, and that maybe I deserve whatever bad thing happens next.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once liked?

Yeah… most days I wake up and it’s just this flat, heavy sadness sitting there. The things that used to kind of reset me don’t really work anymore—putting on a record, cooking something, messing around with electronics.

I mean, I’ll still try sometimes. I have this little soldering kit I used to use for fixing random stuff, and I’ll take it out and then just… stare at it. It’s like the point of it doesn’t reach me anymore.
When did these feelings of sadness and losing interest in things you used to enjoy start? Have they been going on for more than two weeks?

Yeah… definitely more than two weeks. It’s been, I don’t know, about a year and a couple months now. It kind of started after that pipe burst and I had to move into the smaller apartment.

At first I thought it was just the disruption, like all my routines got broken—where I kept things, when I’d cook, even stupid stuff like where the light hits the desk. I kept telling myself I’d settle in, but it just… never really came back.
Have you noticed a big drop in your energy levels or found yourself feeling more tired than usual, even when you’re not doing much?

I’m not totally sure how to measure that. I mean, I get tired, but I don’t know if it’s more than… normal tired? Some days I sit down at the computer and it feels like the whole day disappears, but that could just be because I’m not organizing things right.

It’s funny, I used to keep these little sticky notes lined up by color, and now I’ll find them in drawers or stuck to old mail, which doesn’t answer your question. Sorry. Energy-wise… I guess I haven’t really been paying attention enough to say for sure.
Do you often feel like you’re a failure or that you’ve let people down, even if others might not see it that way?

Yeah… I do. That’s actually a big part of why I’m here, I think.

I keep feeling like I’ve messed things up for everyone—like falling behind at work means other people have to clean up after me, or they’re all noticing how useless I’ve gotten. And with the apartment situation… ever since I lost control of that whole thing, I keep replaying it like I should’ve handled it better.

It’s not even always logical. I’ll be washing a cup or looking for a bill in a pile of mail, and suddenly it’s like, “Of course this is happening. You deserve whatever bad thing comes next.” Then I’ll get distracted by the mail because some of it is still from the old place, and I don’t know why I keep it, but… yeah. I feel like I’ve let people down.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety lately?

Yeah… I think slower, mostly. Not like I’m shuffling around dramatically or anything, but at work I’ll catch myself with my hands just kind of… hovering over the keyboard.

Like a simple support ticket comes in—something I used to answer almost automatically—and I’ll just stare at it, and it takes me longer to type anything back. It feels like my brain and my hands aren’t on the same connection, if that makes sense. Like there’s a delay.

And then I’ll notice the ticket numbers or the formatting or some stupid little thing in the system, and I lose the thread of what I was supposed to be doing. But the main thing is, yeah, I feel slowed down.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or much more than usual?

I don’t really know. I mean, I eat, but I’m not tracking it or anything. Some days I’ll realize it’s late and I haven’t really made a proper meal, but then other days I’ll snack on whatever’s around, so I don’t know if that counts as a change.

My scale is in the bathroom, but there’s this stack of cleaning stuff in front of it because I was going to reorganize the cabinet, and then I didn’t, so I haven’t weighed myself in a while. Clothes seem… about the same, I think. So I guess I haven’t noticed anything clear with appetite or weight.
Have these feelings of sadness and low mood been present most days for at least two years?

No… not two years. It feels long, but if I actually count it, it’s more like a year and a couple months.

It started after that pipe burst and I had to move into the smaller apartment. Everything kind of got thrown off then—my routines, where things were, even stupid stuff like where I kept my chargers and mail—and I guess I never really got back on track. So… about a year and two months, not two years.
Have you found that activities you used to enjoy, like cooking or working with electronics, feel completely pointless or uninteresting to you now?

Yeah… pretty much. I mean, “completely” is a strong word, but most days I wake up and there’s this flat, heavy sadness sitting there before I’ve even done anything.

I’ll think, okay, put on a record, make coffee, maybe cook something decent, and it’s like… none of it gets through. I used to really like messing with old electronics too—taking something apart, figuring out why it wasn’t working—and now I’ll just look at the parts on the table and think, what’s the point?

And then I end up noticing the dust on the shelf, or that one cable I still haven’t labeled, and I’ll spend ten minutes thinking about where I bought it instead of actually doing anything. But yeah… the stuff that used to kind of reset me doesn’t really reach me anymore.
Do you find that even when something good happens, like hearing from a friend or finishing a task, it doesn’t really lift your mood or make you feel better for very long?

Yeah… I think that’s right. Like if a friend texts me, I’ll answer, and for a minute I’ll think, okay, that was nice… but it doesn’t really stick.

Most days I wake up with this flat, heavy sadness already there, and the usual things don’t really break through it. Putting on a record, cooking something, messing with electronics—those used to sort of reset me. Now I might start doing one of them and then notice some tiny thing, like the adapter is in the wrong drawer or the pan I like is still in the sink, and then I’m off thinking about that instead.

So… yeah. Good things happen, but they don’t lift it much, or not for long.
Do you find yourself feeling worthless or guilty almost every day, even about things that wouldn’t have bothered you much before?

Yeah… almost every day, I think. It’s not always loud, but it’s there.

I keep feeling like I’ve ruined things for everyone, especially with falling behind at work and then the whole apartment situation getting out of control. And I know other people deal with worse—my old neighbor had that ceiling leak for weeks and somehow still kept everything together, I don’t know how—but with me it’s like I messed up some basic thing everyone else can handle.

So then I start thinking… maybe I deserve whatever bad thing happens next. Like if something else goes wrong, that’s just what I get.
Before this current period, have you had other times in your life when you felt this same kind of sadness or low mood, and if so, how often did they happen and how long did they last?

I’m… not sure I can pin that down cleanly. I mean, I’ve had bad stretches before, sure, like everybody does, but whether it was this same thing… I don’t know.

There were times I felt low for a while, but I’d have to think about when exactly. My memory sort of turns it into one long file folder, if that makes sense—like when you save things to the desktop and then later you can’t tell what was important and what was just sitting there.

So… I guess I don’t know how often, or for how long. This feels like what I’m dealing with now, but comparing it to before is hard.

Have you ever had a period in your life before this one where you felt persistently sad or lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks, and if so, how many times and how long did they last?

I’m not really sure. I mean… I know there have been stretches where I was down, but whether it was the full two weeks or more, or how many times, I can’t honestly count it.

It all kind of blurs together when I try to look back. Like old work tickets in a queue—some were serious, some were just noise, and after a while you can’t remember which ones took a day and which ones dragged on. So… I don’t want to say yes or no like I know for sure. I just don’t have it organized in my head.
Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period where you felt down or lost interest in things for a couple of weeks or more, where it felt like a real change from your usual self?

I guess… I still don’t really know how to answer that cleanly.

There were times before when I wasn’t myself, maybe, but I can’t tell if it was a couple weeks or just a bad run of days that felt longer. I tend to remember the setting more than the timing, like where I was living or what job I had, not the actual length of it. Like I can remember this one apartment had terrible lighting in the kitchen, but I couldn’t tell you if I was down for ten days or a month then.

So… maybe? But I don’t want to say yes like I’m sure. I just can’t sort it out well enough.

The symptoms have been present for over a year, with no clear remission, and include persistent low mood, anhedonia, feelings of worthlessness and guilt, psychomotor slowing, and significant functional impairment in work and daily living.
